stem: Which substance is transported by aminoacyl-tRNA?
rationale: Each of the 20 amino acids has its own enzyme for this process, termed aminoacyl-tRNA synthetases. These enzymes form an activated intermediate of aminoacyl-AMP–enzyme complex. The specific aminoacyl-AMP–enzyme complex then recognizes a specific tRNA and attaches the aminoacyl moiety at the 3′-hydroxyl adenosyl terminal. The amino acid remains attached to its specific tRNA in an ester linkage until it is incorporated into a polypeptide on the ribosome.

stem: What does EIF-2 act on in the initiation of protein synthesis?
rationale: The first step is the binding of a ternary complex consisting of the initiator methionyl-tRNA (met-tRNAi), GTP, and eIF-2 to the 40S ribosome subunit to form the 43S preinitiation complex.
citation: chapter_37_protein_synthesis_and_the_genetic_code — Protein Synthesis & the Genetic Code > LIKE TRANSCRIPTION, PROTEIN SYNTHESIS CAN BE DESCRIBED IN THREE PHASES: INITIATION, ELONGATION, & TERMINATION > Initiation Involves Several Protein-RNA Complexes

stem: Which substance is transported by the GTP-eIF-2-tRNAi ternary complex?
rationale: The GTP-eIF-2-tRNAi ternary complex binds to the 40S ribosomal subunit to form the 43S preinitiation complex.
citation: chapter_37_protein_synthesis_and_the_genetic_code — Protein Synthesis & the Genetic Code > LIKE TRANSCRIPTION, PROTEIN SYNTHESIS CAN BE DESCRIBED IN THREE PHASES: INITIATION, ELONGATION, & TERMINATION > Formation of the 43S Preinitiation Complex

stem: What is the 43S preinitiation complex converted into?
rationale: The association of mRNA with the 43S preinitiation complex to form the 48S initiation complex requires ATP hydrolysis.
citation: chapter_37_protein_synthesis_and_the_genetic_code — Protein Synthesis & the Genetic Code > LIKE TRANSCRIPTION, PROTEIN SYNTHESIS CAN BE DESCRIBED IN THREE PHASES: INITIATION, ELONGATION, & TERMINATION > Formation of the 48S Initiation Complex

stem: What substance is required by the 43S preinitiation complex to form the 48S initiation complex?
rationale: The association of mRNA with the 43S preinitiation complex to form the 48S initiation complex requires ATP hydrolysis.
citation: chapter_37_protein_synthesis_and_the_genetic_code — Protein Synthesis & the Genetic Code > LIKE TRANSCRIPTION, PROTEIN SYNTHESIS CAN BE DESCRIBED IN THREE PHASES: INITIATION, ELONGATION, & TERMINATION > Formation of the 48S Initiation Complex

stem: What does EIF-5 act on during the binding of the 60S ribosomal subunit to the 48S initiation complex?
rationale: The binding of the 60S ribosomal subunit to the 48S initiation complex involves hydrolysis of the GTP bound to eIF-2 by eIF-5.
citation: chapter_37_protein_synthesis_and_the_genetic_code — Protein Synthesis & the Genetic Code > LIKE TRANSCRIPTION, PROTEIN SYNTHESIS CAN BE DESCRIBED IN THREE PHASES: INITIATION, ELONGATION, & TERMINATION > Formation of the 80S Initiation Complex

stem: What is ATP converted into during the formation of a peptide bond?
rationale: The energy requirements for the formation of one peptide bond include the equivalent of the hydrolysis of two ATP molecules to ADP.
citation: chapter_37_protein_synthesis_and_the_genetic_code — Protein Synthesis & the Genetic Code > LIKE TRANSCRIPTION, PROTEIN SYNTHESIS CAN BE DESCRIBED IN THREE PHASES: INITIATION, ELONGATION, & TERMINATION > Translocation

stem: What is GTP converted into when an aminoacyl-tRNA enters the A site?
rationale: The entry of the aminoacyl-tRNA into the A site results in the hydrolysis of one GTP to GDP.
citation: chapter_37_protein_synthesis_and_the_genetic_code — Protein Synthesis & the Genetic Code > LIKE TRANSCRIPTION, PROTEIN SYNTHESIS CAN BE DESCRIBED IN THREE PHASES: INITIATION, ELONGATION, & TERMINATION > Translocation

stem: Procollagen is converted into which substance?
rationale: Collagen is synthesized as procollagen. Three procollagen polypeptide molecules, which are not always identical in sequence, align in a particular way dependent on specific amino terminal peptides.
citation: chapter_37_protein_synthesis_and_the_genetic_code — Protein Synthesis & the Genetic Code > POSTTRANSLATIONAL PROCESSING AFFECTS THE ACTIVITY OF MANY PROTEINS

stem: What does diphtheria toxin act on in mammalian cells?
rationale: Diphtheria toxin catalyzes the ADP-ribosylation of EF-2. EF-2 contains the unique amino acid diphthamide in mammalian cells.
